subject.title: [Architecture] Migration of transient plugin state to Agent-Scoped SQLite cache tables

question: Should third-party plugin cache state remain in the shared namespaced plugin store, or should the Plugin SDK gain a restricted agent-local cache capability?
rationale: The choice establishes a public Plugin SDK contract and determines agent isolation, backup, migration, expiry, and database ownership; current architecture deliberately places arbitrary plugin state in the global database.

options.title: Keep Global Plugin State
options.body: Use the existing namespaced plugin_state_entries store with TTL, adding documentation or a narrow facade if discoverability is the remaining gap.

options.title: Add Agent-Local Capability
options.body: Design a capability-gated API with explicit agent/session scope, quotas, cleanup, backup, and cross-agent access tests before adding any table or SDK method.

recommendation.title: Keep Global Plugin State
recommendation.body: Use the existing namespaced plugin_state_entries store with TTL, adding documentation or a narrow facade if discoverability is the remaining gap.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on the grouped Plugin SDK session namespace is closest to deciding whether state belongs in that public contract.
